title: Tor vanishing for modules over a localized base ring
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, S a multiplicative submonoid of A and A' a localization of A at S [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Let L and M be A'-modules and j ≥ 0 [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. If Tor^A_j(L,M) vanishes after restricting both modules along A → A', then Tor^{A'}_j(L,M) vanishes. The scalar structures of both modules are the given A'-structures; there is no finite generation assumption.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, (1) to (2), base-ring localization; omitted argument expanded by U4; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B67

proof.text: Let R be restriction of scalars and E extension of scalars. E is additive by its pure-tensor formula and preserves projective objects by the extension/restriction adjunction: R preserves epimorphisms. IsLocalization.flat gives flatness of the restricted localized ring (transported across the identity linear equivalence between its two A-actions). The composite E followed by R is definitionally tensorLeft with that ring, hence preserves finite limits. Since R reflects finite limits, E preserves finite limits, and as a left adjoint E preserves finite colimits. Thus E preserves homology and maps projective resolutions to projective resolutions.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, (1) implies (2), for B in degree zero; used in Tag 069C, lemma-check-perfect-stalks, (1) implies (2); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B67

proof.text: Identify E(R(L)) with L using IsLocalization.moduleLid. Build the natural isomorphism E followed by tensorRight M followed by R to tensorRight R(M): commute the tensor factors over A', cancel the scalar extension using AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange, restrict scalars to A, then commute the tensor factors over A. Naturality is checked by induction on both tensor products; on pure tensors it is definitional equality.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, (1) implies (2), for B in degree zero; used in Tag 069C, lemma-check-perfect-stalks, (1) implies (2); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B67

proof.text: Take Mathlib's projectiveResolution P of R(L) and its image Q = E.mapProjectiveResolution P. Use Q.isoLeftDerivedObj and P.isoLeftDerivedObj to compute both Tor objects. Lift the preceding tensor natural isomorphism to chain complexes with mapHomologicalComplexCompIso. Restriction commutes with homology via mapHomologyIso. These isomorphisms identify the restriction of Tor over A' at E(R(L)), M with Tor over A at R(L), R(M).

proof.text: Transfer h through the homology comparison. Faithfulness of R reflects the zero identity, so the Tor object over A' at E(R(L)), M is zero. Finally map the isomorphism E(R(L)) to L through the derived tensor functor and transfer this zero-object property to the required Tor object. The construction applies uniformly at j = 0, S = {1}, and the zero localization.

theorem isZero_tor_of_restrictScalars_localization
    (A A' : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A']
    (S : Submonoid A) [IsLocalization S A']
    (L M : ModuleCat.{u} A') (j : ℕ)
    (h : IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj
      ((restrictScalars (algebraMap A A')).obj L)).obj
        ((restrictScalars (algebraMap A A')).obj M))) :
    IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A') j).obj L).obj M)
